title: heap-buffer-overflow / SEGV: sqlite3Get4byte reads a page past the buffer
live_proof: fuzz-corpus diff: the image is from SQLite's post-3.22.0 fuzz corpus and reproduces on stock 3.22.0 under host ASan as a heap-buffer-overflow. CORRECTED 2026-10-16: the claim that the report is in sqlite3Get4byte at sqlite3.c:29655 does not hold. Host ASan, re-run on a restored x86 runtime and agreeing with the 2026-10-11 bundle, reports statDecodePage at the free-block chain line -- 253 bytes after a 776-byte region, via statNext <- statNext -- because this image trips an EARLIER over-read in the same statement and ASan aborts at the first one. The sqlite3Get4byte over-read is real and is what both capability arms fault on; ASan simply never reaches it. The re-derivation note on this case and on the CheriBSD copy both assert it 'reproduces at the SAME source line as the log', and that acceptance test is not satisfied
arena_bytes_why: 1 MiB on every arm. Five of the eight spatial cases are forced here by reachability -- at 262144 cases 21, 22 and 23 exhaust memsys5 before the defect (pcache1AllocPage dereferences the NULL that 3.22.0 does not check), 29 returns SQLITE_NOMEM, and 00 takes a different path -- so the same value is declared for all eight to keep the arms comparable. Measured 2026-10-17; this is also the value every recorded virtual reading was taken at, while CheriBSD had been running 262144.
object: the page buffer sqlite3Get4byte reads a 4-byte big-endian value from, reached from statDecodePage. Measured 2026-10-16: the declared site is right and two arms confirm it, Sublet with cause 28 and CheriBSD with PROT_CHERI_BOUNDS, both resolving into sqlite3Get4byte; what is wrong is the claim about which line host ASan reports (see fault_sites_why)
lifetime_ender: not a lifetime defect: a corrupt page header sends the read past the end of the page buffer
shape: read past the end of the record
fidelity: real consumer, real allocator, with a reconstructed trigger. The corpus entry carried only the database and an ASan log -- fuzzcheck pairs every database with every script and the provenance kept only the database id -- so the statement was re-derived by replaying candidate statements one process at a time against a fresh copy of the image. A cumulative script does not work here: an earlier statement leaves the image in a state the later one no longer reaches

status: re-measured on all four readings 2026-10-16 on this platform. host ASan was re-run on a restored x86 runtime: heap-buffer-overflow, 253 bytes after a 776-byte region, statDecodePage <- statNext <- statNext, identical to the 2026-10-11 bundle and NOT in sqlite3Get4byte, see live_proof. virtual-malloc MISSED, RETURNED, both controls as declared -- against the physical spatial row, which reports cause 5 load out of bounds; the two builds disagree, see note. virtual-nested-pools CAUGHT, cause=28 pc=0x3f9c86ad20 in sqlite3Get4byte, both controls as declared. cheribsd-revocation CAUGHT: SIGPROT(34) si_code=1 PROT_CHERI_BOUNDS, valid-cap-out-of-bounds, pc=0x14272c resolving to sqlite3Get4byte+16, with the image loaded (s0_rc=11, database disk image is malformed) and the boot positive control trapping. THE CHERIBSD READING CHANGES, AND NOT BECAUSE OF THE MECHANISM. The nine spatial cases were all recorded not-detected on 2026-10-06, and those readings were taken without their corrupt database images present -- the silent failure found while reviewing case 21 and fixed in e9199203, where sqlite3_open creates an empty database, the first statement returns 'no such table' and the case prints RETURNED rc=0. With the images restored on 2026-10-16, on the same binaries and the same arm, this case faults. The 10-06 TSV records it as PASS. The arms block is the 2026-10-11 bundle's and is regenerated by derive-verdicts.py when this review ends. RE-MEASURED 2026-10-17 with one arena on every arm (arena_bytes=1048576) and every arm built from the corpus case.c: virtual-malloc MISSED, virtual-nested-pools CAUGHT cause=28 pc=0x3f9506ad20 in sqlite3Get4byte, cheribsd-revocation MISSED with RETURNED rc=0 and probe site 64 reporting hits=608 witnesses=557 -- reached and silent, not a no-reading. The earlier spatial readings were taken with the virtual arms at a 1 MiB header default against CheriBSD's 262144, and with this arm compiling its own copy of the case
note: Re-measured 2026-10-16. The case is real and its declared site is right, but three records needed correcting and one verdict changes. (1) The CheriBSD cell goes from MISSED to CAUGHT, for the reason in status: the 2026-10-06 reading was taken without the image. The new fault is SIGPROT si_code=1, PROT_CHERI_BOUNDS -- a bounds violation on a VALID capability, categorically different from the si_code=2 tag faults that every false positive in this review turned out to be -- and it resolves into sqlite3Get4byte, the declared site, which is also where the Sublet arm faults with cause 28. Probe site 64 shows why a malloc-granularity mechanism can see this one at all: the over-read runs far enough to leave the WHOLE 256 KiB arena, the witness reporting kind=CAP-OOB with cb=<arena>+262144 and ca past its end. An over-read that stays inside the arena is invisible there, which is why the other spatial cases are silent on that arm. (2) live_proof claimed host ASan reports sqlite3Get4byte at sqlite3.c:29655. It does not: ASan reports statDecodePage at the free-block chain line, because this image trips an earlier over-read in the same statement and ASan aborts at the first one. Both the corpus note and the CheriBSD copy assert the re-derived trigger reproduces at the same source line as the original log, and that acceptance test is not satisfied. The sqlite3Get4byte over-read is nonetheless real: two independent capability arms fault there. (3) The two base builds disagree. The physical spatial row reports cause 5, load out of bounds, and the virtual-malloc build completes. That is the same build-dependence case 20 showed, but here in the direction of a genuine mechanism rather than a forged pointer: base Capstone holds the arena as one capability, so an over-read is visible exactly when it leaves the arena, and where it lands relative to the arena end differs between builds. The published cell is D, from the physical row, and it is a real bounds fault; what cannot be claimed is that it would fire on any build. (4) Probe site 64 hooks all three unchecked reads in statDecodePage and separates this case from 31 and 32: here the free-block chain runs once with iOff=1027 and the CELL walk runs 613 times reaching iOff=52996, where 31 takes the cell walk to 64768 in 8 iterations and 32 takes the free-block chain to 17234. The three images exercise two different unguarded reads, so despite 29 and 32 sharing an ASan line they are not duplicates -- measured, not inferred from the stacks, which is what the 00-against-25 check taught
fault_sites_why: Host ASan, running the same case source on stock 3.22.0, reports the invalid access in sqlite3Get4byte (live_proof); that run is independent of the Capstone arms and predates them.
